articleTitle: New Efficiency: Introducing Social Assistive Robots in Social Eldercare Organizations
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Innovation and Entrepreneurship (TEMS-ISIE)
abstract: This paper continues to develop the fundamental requirements of a living lab as social experiment on the multistage integration of Social Assistive Robots in an AAL environment with caregiver capacity shortage and elder people living with different physical and mental stages. Starting from the results of a pre-study conducted on 130 dependent living elderly in Austria retirement houses, this paper presents a process-costs-calculation of Social Assistive Robots (SAR) introduction in the process of eldercare ("CareSAR") and suggests a program to optimize the benefit of these solutions under the aspects of shortage of caregivers, high quality of medical care and ethics.

articleTitle: Quality Dimensions in Health Care Units in selected states of India An exploratory Study using SERVQUAL
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Innovation and Entrepreneurship (TEMS-ISIE)
abstract: The objective of this paper is to investigate the patients as customers, patient satisfaction and its determinants, measurement issues in health care units of India an exploratory approach. As the empirical study using five dimensions of SERQUAL in various cities covering three states of India Telangana, Chhattisgarh and Himachal Pradesh. A total of 120 responses from patients as customers and 45 responses from doctors. A seven point scale was used to investigate the results. The results reported are used by the health care units to refine, restructure to enhance quality management issues and for the future directions. This work helps in designing effective healthcare quality strategies in hospitals gap analysis has also been done. This report also identifies some discomfort in the patient services quality of the hospital for further improvements as an exploratory approach.

articleTitle: Relationship Between Proactive Personality and Employee Well-Being: Mediating Effect of Psychological Capital
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Innovation and Entrepreneurship (TEMS-ISIE)
abstract: Proactive personality scale, psychological capital questionnaire and employee well-being questionnaire are adopted in the research, and employees are investigated through network questionnaire. Data are analyzed for exploring the relationship between proactive personality and employee wellbeing as well as the mediating effect of psychological capital. The result showed that employee proactive personality can be applied for significant forward prediction of employee wellbeing and psychological capital; psychological capital can be applied for significant forward prediction of employee wellbeing; psychological capital has complete mediating effect between proactive personality and employee well-being.

articleTitle: Contextual Factors Affecting Decisions About Intellectual Property Licensing Provisions in Collaboration Agreements for Open Innovation Projects of Complex Technological Organizations
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Innovation and Entrepreneurship (TEMS-ISIE)
abstract: Firms collaborate with partners in research and development (R&D) of new technologies for many reasons such as to access complementary knowledge, know-how or skills, to seek new opportunities outside their traditional technology domain, to sustain their continuous flows of innovation, to reduce time to market, or to share risks and costs [1]. The adoption of collaborative research agreements (CRAs) or collaboration agreements (CAs) is rising rapidly as firms attempt to access innovation from various types of organizations to enhance their traditional in-house innovation [2], [3]. To achieve the objectives of their collaborations, firms need to share knowledge and jointly develop new knowledge. As more firms adopt open collaborative innovation strategies, intellectual property (IP) management has inevitably become important because clear and fair contractual IP terms and conditions such as IP ownership allocation, licensing arrangements and compensation for IP access are required for each collaborative project [4], [5]. Moreover, the firms need to adjust their IP management strategies to fit the unique characteristics and circumstances of each particular project [5].

articleTitle: Strategic Orientation and Innovation Ecosystem Structure
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Innovation and Entrepreneurship (TEMS-ISIE)
abstract: It is noticed that there is heterogeneity in the structure of innovation ecosystems, however, what are the actual differences of innovation ecosystem structures and the causes of such differences remain unexplored. This study adopts a multi-case analysis method, explores two types of innovation ecosystem structures from a micro level, and suggests strategic orientation as an important factor that influence innovation ecosystem structure, This study contributes to the literature of innovation ecosystem structure and provides implication for enterprises.

articleTitle: Design And Prospect Of New Splicing Heterogeneous Chips
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Innovation and Entrepreneurship (TEMS-ISIE)
abstract: The new heterogeneous chip will become the development direction of the future chip field, which includes the existing chip computing capabilities, and combines branches of many different computing fields such as quantum computing and DNA biometrics computing. In particular, the great potential of such heterogeneous computing is pointed out, especially if the channel capacity expansion of communication is considered, the implementation of the three-dimensional heterogeneous stacked chip can be further considered. In this paper, a novel splicing chip architecture will be proposed to implement this heterogeneous chip. Its idea comes from the brain-like computing chip architecture, but it has been further developed in this article. The application potential of the splicing architecture in the new heterogeneous chip is discussed in depth from the perspective of connectivity and redundancy tolerance.

articleTitle: Corporate Political Strategy and Performance Fluctuations in a Transitional Economy —Empirical Evidence from Chinese Listed Companies
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Innovation and Entrepreneurship (TEMS-ISIE)
abstract: The imperfect institution of transitional economies provides many opportunities for companies to develop various political strategies, but what is a better way to implement these corporate political strategies (CPSs) to improve firm value. By combining institutional theory and resource dependence theory, this paper sheds light on the different impact of CPSs implemented on the institutional level (InsCPS) and the individual level (IndCPS) on performance fluctuations, which is an important dimension of firm value. Moreover, we explore the contingent effect of government's role. Based on a date set of Chinese listed companies, our empirical results suggest that (1) InsCPSs contribute more to a lower the fluctuation of corporate performance, compared with IndCPS; (2) when there are more government supports for the local business, the contribution of InsCPSs to a lower fluctuation will be greater. Our findings deepen the understanding of the CPS-firm value relationship, and also provide theoretical implications for maintaining sustainable government-business relationship in a transitional economy.

articleTitle: Current Situation, Problems and Solutions of Colleges’ Talents Cultivation Scheme Reform under the policy of "Emerging Engineering Education"
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Innovation and Entrepreneurship (TEMS-ISIE)
abstract: A lot of efforts has been put into invigorating the talents cultivation scheme in universities with the emerging policy of "Emerging Engineering Education". This study aims to examine the status quo of colleges’ talents cultivation scheme in Tianjin University by virtue of various approaches such as case study, field work, questionnaire and interview. Based on the analysis of Triple Helix Theory, the study evaluates typical cases and further proposes implications for colleges to promote cross-disciplinary exploration from aspects of construction of platform, institutional assurance and Brand activities.

articleTitle: Circular Economy: Challenges and Potentials for the Manufacturing Industry by Digital Transformation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Innovation and Entrepreneurship (TEMS-ISIE)
abstract: The world is steering towards a situation, where resource scarcity will result in cost explosion of material and governments are overstrained to dispose the constantly accumulating amount of waste in their countries. One way to overcome the resulting challenges is the implementation of a circular system, in order to create a closed material cycle and eliminate the production of further waste. The ongoing digital transformation offers the potential to enable a transition towards a circular economy. Therefore, recent studies have been examined, which advocate that digital technologies are key enabling factors to realize the shift from a linear to a circular system. Despite this general agreement, the literature still neglects how digital technologies enable such a circular economy transition for the manufacturing industry. To fill the gap, this paper presents a research framework comprising nine success factors, based on digital transformation technologies. The research framework is composed of two dimensions. The first dimension describes the three phases (manufacturing, usage and reutilization/recycling) of a product lifecycle. The second dimension depicts the design levels of business engineering (strategic-, system- and information level). Therefore, the nine success factors have been described for each level of the framework along the product lifecycle in the context of digital transformation. Thus, the paper gives recommendations to overcome the challenges of manufacturing companies concerning the realization of a circular economy.

articleTitle: 5G, Dynamic Capabilities and Business Models Innovation in Healthcare industry
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Innovation and Entrepreneurship (TEMS-ISIE)
abstract: 5G technologies pose new challenges and provide opportunities, especially for industries like healthcare, where data and mobile remote communication play an important role in organizations' ability to provide value-based services. Hospitals are therefore in need of innovating their business models to incorporate 5G-enabled opportunities. Our discussion highlights the mediating mechanisms by which dynamic capabilities and business models influence each other, clarifying what determines business-model innovation in an organizational setting. The premise of this research is that hospitals demonstrate emerging business model patterns that reflect a combination of their capabilities and the type of innovation involved. This paper develops a conceptual framework and presents four cases gathered from hospitals to unveil key ingredients of business models required for 5G-enabled healthcare services.

articleTitle: Practices of Innovation Management Enabling Technology Adoption and Diffusion at the Grassroots
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Innovation and Entrepreneurship (TEMS-ISIE)
abstract: Innovation taking at the grassroots level has the ability to furnish bottom-up solutions that acknowledge the local issues, interest by solving problems related to economic, social and environmental situations for underdeveloped communities. The objective of this study is to analyze the innovation management framing and technology adoption and dissemination from a voluntary organization working at the grassroots level in the Indian Subcontinent. The study analyses the local innovation practices and ecosystem, the role played by the local organization in empowerment of rural communities enabling an inclusive development. A case based method was adopted where primary data are taken from interview with the innovators, community members. The study gives an insight into how the innovation management at the grassroots are framed through various mechanism such as learning practices, participatory design, technology transfer. The findings of the study revealed four themes such as Capacity Building, Women Empowerment, Creation of entrepreneurial opportunity, Technology transfer for promoting Sustainability.

articleTitle: Presenting an Iterative Innovation Framework Perceived for Resource-Constrained Society
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Innovation and Entrepreneurship (TEMS-ISIE)
abstract: In the literature, innovation-related issues are widely discussed in the context of large firms/industrialized nations. However, case-based studies to explore the determinant factors in the success/failure of technological innovation for resource-constrained societies are still inadequate and evolving. Hence, this article presents an exploratory case study to examine an equitable, sustainable and democratic product innovation and management framework evolving under Rural Technology Action Group (RuTAG) in India. Three special cases of RuTAG are considered here as a case study. We have adopted the multi-method approach research tools viz. workshops, idea-sharing sessions, end users' opinion collection, etc. so that all the stakeholders' judgments can be collected and analyzed to get a clear insight into the product innovation process emerging under the RuTAG project. Based on those insights, we have presented here an iterative innovation management framework. The key features of the framework are the participation of stakeholders in each iteration so that academia can collect real-time feedback from users to accommodate social needs/circumstances/financial and infrastructure capacities in the development and delivery of the product. Moreover, this study will try to map different actors and explore their roles in the process of overcoming the barriers to successful product innovation which are generally missing in traditional innovation practices. Thus, we seek to understand how a complex network of actors in the RuTAG project helps in the design, development, and transfer of need-based products/technologies in a resource-constrained society. Further, the feedback-gathering mechanism developed by RuTAG to collect a community's needs/ aspirations/ constraints about products/ technology is presented.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence for Innovation Readiness Assessment
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Innovation and Entrepreneurship (TEMS-ISIE)
abstract: There are two main necessities for an innovation to become successful. Firstly, there must be a target market willing to buy the innovation and secondly, the technology must be ready to deliver. The READINESSnavigator is a state of the art software tool that packages an innovation readiness assessment methodology that is proven to increase success chances for innovations. Usage of the READINESSnavigator has shown, that it works best if there is somebody to explain the method. This paper outlines our approach to automate this individual using artificial intelligence. To do so, it outlines the history of innovation readiness assessment methods, artificial intelligence and explains the high-level architecture of an automated innovation coach.

articleTitle: Blockchain-Based Open Network in Technology Intermediation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Innovation and Entrepreneurship (TEMS-ISIE)
abstract: Blockchain technology is developing using in reliable applications which can be designed to achieve decentralization and trustless. Based on the open network innovation theory, this paper proposes a technical intermediary management idea based on blockchain technology to improve the efficiency of technology intermediaries, providing accurate, reliable information and cutting cost for the market. This study demonstrates the advantage of blockchain to technology intermediaries. First, on a specific level, it can provide openness, transparency, decentralization and anonymity services. Second, the current industrial innovation elements are analyzed. blockchain improve the efficiency of technology intermediary, prevent risks and to make up for the shortcomings of traditional intermediaries. It has revolutionized the traditional technology intermediary. As this happens, it can revolutionize traditional technology intermediaries.

articleTitle: Organizational Flexibility from the Perspective of the Creation of Cooperation Networks in Family Businesses
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Innovation and Entrepreneurship (TEMS-ISIE)
abstract: The contemporary conditions for the operations of enterprises, including family businesses, require a high level of organizational flexibility in the market decisions taken. This also applies to the creation of cooperation networks since the benefits from adopting the cooperation strategy provides enterprises with competitive advantage in turbulent and demanding markets. The objective of the article is to diagnose the level of flexible operations from the perspective of the creation of cooperation networks between organizations in the market. The conducted analysis is based on the own research results on a group of Polish family businesses. During the analysis, appropriate statistical methods were used, the application of which allowed for indicating the relationships and conditions of the level of flexibility of operations.

articleTitle: Research on the Influencing Factors of Leading Technology Diffusion Based on Technology Acceptance Model
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Innovation and Entrepreneurship (TEMS-ISIE)
abstract: With the increasing use of traditional energy in the world, the problems of traditional energy exhaustion, environmental pollution and unsustainability are aggravated. Many countries in the world have turned their attention to the development of new energy and tried to find a clean, pollution-free and sustainable way. Therefore, the technology diffusion in the new energy industry has attracted more and more attention. This paper uses technology acceptance model to explore the influencing factors of technology diffusion in new energy industry: technology acceptance, technology readiness. We also use perceived usefulness and perceived ease of use to measure the relationship between technology acceptance and adoption behavior, which verified the positive correlation between technology acceptance and technology diffusion in new energy industry, as well as the regulatory role of Technology readiness. Meanwhile, in order to promote the effective diffusion of new energy industry leading technology, we give relevant countermeasures and suggestions from the perspective of enterprises and government based on the empirical results.

articleTitle: Communication and Trust as Facilitators for Collaborative Innovation Development in Virtual Teams
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Innovation and Entrepreneurship (TEMS-ISIE)
abstract: In this study, we investigate how relationship communication affects the innovation / creativity process in a virtual environment. We propose a multiple mediator model in which cognitive and affective trust act as mediating mechanisms that transmit the positive effects of communication to innovation/creativity development within teams. The main results of this study revealed significant positive correlations between relationship communication, trust and innovation / creativity. In addition, this study identified interpersonal trust as playing an important role in mediating the relation between relationship communication and innovation/creativity. Both the emotional aspect of trust and the rational aspect have proven to be mediators of innovation / creativity. These findings contribute to solve some of the emerging organizational challenges through a better understanding of the innovation development mechanism.

articleTitle: Technology Development and Applying Scenary of UAV: A Patentometric Survey
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Innovation and Entrepreneurship (TEMS-ISIE)
abstract: Being strengthened by advances of industrial technology as well as improvement of supply chains, demanded by civil markets and national defense, cultivated by social and economic forces, oriented by national policies and regulations, UAV technology is meeting a huge chance in terms of applying scenarioes and potential markets. Aimming to draw a panorama of UAV R&D to recognize further opportunities of technical innovation and challenges for organizations in industrial chains, value chains and innovative systems around UAV technology R&D and manufacture, an analysis based on a patentometric survey was initially carried out. Furthermore, expectations on applying opportunities and R&D directions were concluded for potential applicants based on patentometric evidences and on the environmental analysis, for the latter the logistics industry was chosen as a case.

articleTitle: Ideas and opportunities: Impact of technology knowledge through entrepreneurial alertness
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Innovation and Entrepreneurship (TEMS-ISIE)
abstract: Not all ideas are opportunities. Clear differentiation between the two concepts are vital to our understanding of the entrepreneurial opportunity recognition process. How does certain knowledge of information transform to be an idea or a feasible opportunity? The purpose of this study is to examine the relationships of technology knowledge and opportunity recognition process of small firms technology firms in Malaysia. The study seeks to explore the gaps in our current knowledge on the opportunity recognition process for ideas and for exploitation of opportunities. This paper employs quantitative research design involving self-reporting questionnaires. Founders and co-founders of technology companies (n=255) are surveyed as respondents and data collected are analyzed using PLS-SEM technique. Findings have shown that technology knowledge affect the entrepreneur's ability to recognize opportunity. Technology knowledge influences directly providing ideas for further exploration. From a more practical standpoint, the use of ideation programs in entrepreneurial initiatives needs to be clear on the outcomes of the program and to further supplement with the right support for full exploitation of opportunities. The clear delineation of the opportunity construct within the entrepreneurship studies enables progress to be made in building a clearer opportunity recognition framework. The empirical results are also supporting the presence of entrepreneurial alertness as the mediator in the model. This relationship not been explored and empirically proven previously.

articleTitle: Comparison of Entrepreneurial Activities of 31 Provincial Regions in China: Clustering Analysis of Multi-Indicator Cross-section Data
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Innovation and Entrepreneurship (TEMS-ISIE)
abstract: There are large differences in the level of entrepreneurial activity and the degree of development in various regions of China. In order to effectively classify the level of entrepreneurial activities in various regions of China, this study adopts cross-section data of 31 provincial regions, uses multi-dimension indicators to measure and assess the entrepreneurial characteristics of different regional clusters.

articleTitle: Alliance Management Capability of Entrepreneurial Nonprofit Organizations and Cross-sector Alliance Performance: An fsQCA Approach
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Innovation and Entrepreneurship (TEMS-ISIE)
abstract: An overarching configuration perspective of alliance management capabilities (AMC) is ignored in the realm of cross-sector alliance research. This study fills this gap by exploring how AMC underpin the successful and greater performance of cross-sector alliances. This study examines four dimensions of AMC that affect the performance of crosssector alliance, viz., social impact realizing, relationship coordination, power balancing and inter-organizational learning, from the perspective of nonprofit organizations (NPOs). Based on a survey to socially entrepreneurial nonprofit organizations and their cross-sector alliances in tourism industry in China, this study uses the method of fuzzyset qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA) to investigate the connection between configuration of AMC and high alliance performance. The findings identify three solutions of different elements configuration of AMC leading to high cross-sector alliance performance. The findings have some theoretical contributions and practical implications for cross-sector alliance management.

articleTitle: Technology Complementarity and Collaborative Innovation: The Moderating Effects of IT Adoption
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Innovation and Entrepreneurship (TEMS-ISIE)
abstract: This paper studies the influence of technology complementarity between partners on firm's collaborative innovation, as well as the boundary condition of that relationship. We test our hypotheses using partial least squares (PLS). The results show that both technology complementarity relates positively to firm's collaborative innovation. Our results also indicate that IT adoption has significant moderating role on the effects technology complementarity. Our research has important implications for research in collaborative innovation.

articleTitle: Empirical Study on the Relationship Between Subjective Well-being of Employees and Social Performance in Social Enterprises
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Innovation and Entrepreneurship (TEMS-ISIE)
abstract: Social enterprises are emerging enterprises that adopt commercial methods to solve social problems. However, previous studies have not studied the impact of employee characteristics on organizational performance. Under the background of China, this paper use 52.social enterprises and 270 employees as samples to verify the relationship between emotional commitment and subjective well-being of employees in social enterprises and social performance of enterprises by using multilevel structural equation model (MSEM). The study found that: life satisfaction and emotional balance, have a significant role in promoting affective commitment, and also have a significant role in promoting social performance of enterprises; affective commitment plays a mediating role between life satisfaction, emotional balance and social performance of enterprises.

articleTitle: Entrepreneurial Orientation in Organizational Culture of Small Enterprise
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Innovation and Entrepreneurship (TEMS-ISIE)
abstract: The concept of entrepreneurial orientation, as a concept at the enterprise level, can be located in the organizational culture, creating a specific standard of this culture. If this standard is perceived as having high quality (intensity), one can speak about an entrepreneurial culture. The main aim of the article is the diagnosis of the relations between entrepreneurial orientation and its implementation in the organizational culture. The hypothesis was empirically tested with questionnaire survey data obtained in 2018 from 260 small enterprises in Poland. As a main conclusion, the entrepreneurial culture of small enterprises is based on entrepreneurial orientation dimensions to a different degree, which confirms the assumption of the multidimensionality of the construct. Small enterprises base their entrepreneurial culture to the greatest extent on proactivity and innovation, which are also the best aware elements of the entrepreneurial culture of the surveyed enterprises.

articleTitle: R&D Partner Type, Product Life-cycle, and Innovation Performance of High-technology Ventures
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Innovation and Entrepreneurship (TEMS-ISIE)
abstract: To cope with rapidly changing market demand and deficiency of internal resources, innovative ventures actively invite various types of external partners to their innovation process. Although many research has been conducted to identify the effect of R&D partner types on firm performances, few studies have taken into account venture firm as well as the stage of the product life-cycle in examining the issue, which can significantly affect the strategic decision on and the outcome of R&D collaboration. To this end, this study focuses on high-technology ventures at three different stages in product life-cycle and examines the effect of R&D collaboration with five different types of R&D partner on innovation performance of ventures. Our findings reveal that for ventures in the introduction stage, R&D collaboration with large firm is positively related to their innovation performance. In the growth stage of product life-cycle, R&D collaborations with university, public research institute (PRI), and large firm are positively associated with innovation performance. Lastly, for ventures in the mature stage of product life-cycle, university and public research institute are suggested as effective partners for innovation performance of ventures. Neither R&D collaboration with private research centers (PRC) nor other SMEs and ventures show a significant effect on innovation performance at all three stages of product life-cycle. This research contributes to the existing literature of open innovation and innovation management of ventures.

articleTitle: Knowledge Stock, Competition Orientation and Latecomer Firms’ Attention to Emerging Technologies
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Innovation and Entrepreneurship (TEMS-ISIE)
abstract: Based on the company's attention-based view, this paper takes the Chinese A-share listed companies in the computer and communication industry in 2012-2017 as a sample to explore the impact of the late-stage enterprise knowledge stock and competition-oriented attention on its emerging technologies. The empirical results show that the knowledge stock is negatively related to the company's attention to emerging technologies; enterprises with cost-oriented firms as the rules of action will pay less attention to emerging technologies. This study has important theoretical and practical significance for clarifying the determinants of the emerging technology attention distribution of late-developing enterprises.

articleTitle: Gender Diversity and Entrepreneurship
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Innovation and Entrepreneurship (TEMS-ISIE)
abstract: Crowdfunding has become an important source of capital for entrepreneurship, and it may further challenge the mediate role of traditional financial system. We document the crowdfunding activities initiated by Chinese entrepreneurs on the "colorful investment" platform (from the platform beginning to 2019) and analyze the influence of entrepreneur team gender diversity on crowdfunding performance. The results show that teams with higher gender diversity will set lower campaign goal amounts and receive lower actual financing. We believe that the most likely explanation for these differences is that women's risk aversion preference. Suggesting a tendency to take less risk activities, we find that entrepreneur team with higher gender diversity (more women) tend to set lower goal amounts and are more likely to achieve higher pledged amounts relative to campaign goals.

articleTitle: Exploration of Scientific and Technological Innovation Path of Enterprises in China
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Innovation and Entrepreneurship (TEMS-ISIE)
abstract: China has been claimed to be a major-power country developing by leaps and bounds. "Innovation" became one of our main development concepts. It is of great significance to effectively promote industrial upgrading and transformation, enhance enterprise efficiency and broaden enterprise development space. First, based on the benchmarking method, this paper analyzes the policy and practice investment of scientific and technological innovation in developed countries such as the United States, Britain and Germany in recent years, and summarizes the characteristics of scientific and technological development stage in China, inspiring the future development. Additionally, by means of literature study, expert interview and text mining and analytics etc., this paper attempts to promote the science and technology innovation as the core and further support the research of related topics at the enterprise level, putting forward the development path of science and technology innovation at medium and micro level.

articleTitle: Cost Reduction First or Innovation First? Latecomer Firms’ Technology Catching-up Strategy Selection
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Innovation and Entrepreneurship (TEMS-ISIE)
abstract: Based on the composition-based view (CBV), this paper studies the effect of cost-oriented and innovation-oriented catching-up strategies on the performance of latecomer firms by taking 249 A-share listed firms in the communication and electronic equipment manufacturing industry as samples. In addition, the paper examines the moderating effect of the technological knowledge stock on the relationship between the choice of catching-up strategy and the performance of latecomer firms. The study has found that the more the latecomer firms focus on reducing costs, the higher the performance; the more the latecomer firms emphasize innovation, the lower the performance. In addition, the high technological knowledge stock of latecomer firms can weaken the positive relationship between the cost-oriented strategy and the firm performance, but it has no effect on the negative relationship between the innovation-oriented strategy and the firm performance. The research results have a certain reference value for the selection of catching-up strategies of latecomer firms.

articleTitle: Innovation Ecosystems for Sustainability Transition: From Policy Intervention to Stakeholder Coalition
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Innovation and Entrepreneurship (TEMS-ISIE)
abstract: In this paper I develop and compare two models of innovation. Following literature review a conventional model of technological innovation is constructed which focuses primarily on new product or new process development. In recent years through my research, teaching and editorial experience, I develop an emerging model of innovation ecosystems which offer a broader framework for innovation studies. I use the automotive industry as a case in point and argue that technological innovation to reduce CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> emissions from the transport sector has been primarily driven by policy interventions as exogenous forces. Innovation ecosystems are a more effective approach to helping us embark on the transition to sustainability. Key to innovation ecosystems are stakeholder coalition, a combination of both exogenous and endogenous forces to innovation ecosystems. Considering the relative efficiency of innovation development by product producers vs. product intermediate users I conclude that product intermediate users augmented innovation ecosystem is more effective and efficient than policy-intervention model.
